rdf:Description.dc:title: Executive Order 8802
rdf:Description.dc:description: On June 25, 1941, President Franklin Roosevelt signed Executive Order 8802 which prohibited racial and other discrimination in the defense industry. The Executive Order was a partial response by the White House to a planned march by African American activists on the National Mall to protest discrimination in the defense industry. Defense jobs were a major source of employment even though the United States was not yet at war.
